brief: A system monitor where CPU/memory are organisms — healthy breathes steady, stressed pulses fast

dominant_strengths: Strong conceptual metaphor: cells as organisms with green particles reads as living, distinctive systems thinking.
Color split between calm amber and stressed red carries emotional state without needing labels.
Visceral first impression is striking against the deep navy void, evoking microscope diagnostics.
dominant_weaknesses: Composition is unbalanced — left tooltip floats orphaned, two cells drift in empty space with weak anchoring.
Data legibility is poor: which organism is CPU vs memory is ambiguous, no labels tie metrics to cells.
Connection line between organisms is faint and purposeless, undermining the relational story it implies.
fix_priorities: Label each organism (CPU, Memory) directly and bind the stat panel to its cell via proximity or leader line.
Rebalance canvas — tighten spacing, give the two cells a shared baseline and breathing rhythm reference.
Strengthen the inter-cell connection with meaningful flow (data packets, pulse sync) or remove it entirely.
Add a subtle scale/grid so 'pulse fast vs breathe steady' is readable as motion, not just static color.
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral and reflective pull from the organism metaphor, but behavioral utility lags because the readout doesn't clearly map metrics to the visuals.
rationale.intent_fit: The metaphor lands conceptually, but without clear identification and motion cues it functions more as poster than working monitor.
